intro: These are the items that could not be confirmed, or where a source contradicts itself. They are published here rather than guessed at, and they do NOT block any decision — each has a stated resolution path.

items.item: Exact lease expiry date and the remaining rent, escalations and renewal options
items.why_flagged: The principal supplied only a 2030-2035 window and no lease document. Any value figure depends on these, so none is stated anywhere on this site.
items.resolution: Provide the executed lease and amendments (internal use only).

items.item: The actual in-place NOI, pricing, and therefore the 'sell now' value
items.why_flagged: Without rent (F-01) and without a certified appraisal, no sale value can be stated. Market cap-rate evidence (T07) is third-party and brand-wide, not parcel-specific.
items.resolution: Order an MAI appraisal or broker BOV on the actual lease terms.

items.item: The parcel's Fire Hazard Severity Zone and Alquist-Priolo/seismic zone status
items.why_flagged: CAL FIRE and CGS publish parcel-level maps, but the parcel number is withheld under the privacy policy, so the specific classification could not be looked up. Only the existence of the regulatory programmes is asserted.
items.resolution: Look up the parcel in the CAL FIRE FHSZ viewer and CGS EQ Zapp using the APN; record the result internally.

items.item: A broker flyer used for market context contradicts itself on the lease expiry
items.why_flagged: The flyer's header states 'Lease Expiration: July 31, 2036' while its investment-highlights paragraph states the lease 'expires July 31, 2031'. Only its asking cap rate (4.31%) is used, and only as a market data point.
items.resolution: Treat that flyer as marketing material, not evidence; use it only for the cap rate.

items.item: Two Los Angeles-area cap rates in the third-party evidence are not like-for-like
items.why_flagged: The 4.31% figure is an absolute-NNN corporate lease with roughly 15 years of term; the 5.82% figure is a ground lease with about 13 years of term. They are not the same asset structure, so averaging them would be wrong.
items.resolution: Report both with their structures attached (done on the Market Pricing page) and never average them.

items.item: Jack in the Box issuer credit rating (S&P / Moody's)
items.why_flagged: No official rating was found on the SEC filings reviewed, and the third-party aggregator page shows 'N/A' for both agencies. A rating is therefore not asserted.
items.resolution: Check the rating agencies directly, or rely on the filed financials (T06) which are official.

items.item: Whether the lease is a corporate lease or a franchisee lease with a guaranty
items.why_flagged: Not supplied by the principal. This materially changes the tenant-credit conclusion (R01): a franchisee lease is materially weaker than a corporate one.
items.resolution: Read the lease preamble and guaranty pages.

items.item: City-level building permits and employer-establishment counts
items.why_flagged: Census QuickFacts reports 'X' (not applicable/available) for Los Angeles city on Building Permits 2025 and the 2023 business counts. County-level values are published and are used instead.
items.resolution: Use the county series, or query the Census Building Permits Survey and County Business Patterns directly for the city.

items.item: Forward population projection for the trade area
items.why_flagged: The California Department of Finance publishes county projections (S12) as Excel/CSV attachments that could not be parsed in this environment, so no forward population figure is published. The projection landing page was verified, the numbers were not.
items.resolution: Download P-2A County Total Population and quote the Los Angeles County row directly.

items.item: Insurance cost and availability for the parcel
items.why_flagged: No official source publishes commercial property insurance premiums by parcel. The post-wildfire repricing described in R08 is documented only as a qualitative regulatory fact (FHSZ maps), not as a price series.
items.resolution: Obtain a current insurance quote and the tenant's certificate of insurance.

items.item: FRED series named 'LAPOP' is Louisiana, not Los Angeles
items.why_flagged: During research, the series LAPOP was initially assumed to measure Los Angeles population; its own metadata shows it is 'Resident Population in Louisiana'. It was discarded. No value from it appears on this site. Flagged so future sessions do not repeat the error.
items.resolution: Use Census QuickFacts (S05/S06) for Los Angeles population.

items.item: SEIU/tenant level unit sales for the specific store
items.why_flagged: Store-level sales would materially improve the renewal rent argument (OPT-C) but are confidential tenant data and were not available. Renewal economics are therefore framed qualitatively.
items.resolution: Request unit-level AUV and P&L from the tenant under NDA.
